newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices fall 3/4 to a point.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices fall 3/4 to a point.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices fell 3/4 of a point to a point by midday, sympathizing with U.S. Treasury bonds' sharper skid after Friday's robust employment report.
"In general the (muni) market is off seven to eight basis points," a trader said, adding that the market appeared to have stabilized at the adjusted levels.
The Labor Department said the U.S. economy created 262,000 jobs in December, versus economists' predictions of a 192,000 gain.
The trader said municipals seemed to hold up fairly well considering the drubbing sustained by Treasuries, where the 30-year bond was down 1-5/8 at 95-5/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
"There seems to be some bargain hunting or bottom fishing at the adjusted levels," he said.
The trader said Thursday's high trade on 30-year New York City paper was at a 6.28 percent yield, while bonds traded Friday at a 6.36 percent yield.
"So that's down eight basis points," he said.
Thirty-year New York State Dormitory Authority paper traded Thursday in the 6.07 to 6.08 percent yield range, the trader said.
"And today there was a trade on bonds at a 6.15," he said.
Thirty-year Puerto Rico paper was weaker by about seven basis points, the trader said. Thursday's high trade as at a 5.84 percent yield, while Friday's low trade was at a 5.91 percent yield.
Most of the activity taking place was in index bonds, the trader said.

"Obviously (for) the longer stuff that's more contract related, index-type bonds, there are markets, two sided markets," the trader said. "I can't tell you if anything is actually trading, I think it's more on quotes than actual transactions."
The trader said while bids existed, "to be honest with you, I think if you actually tried to hit some of these bids, I don't think they would take the bonds."
On the bright side, aside from a single list of about $100 million, customer selling was limited, he said.

"I think there are people who are reluctant to sell at these lower levels, and I don't know if they'd give up the ghost next week, but certainly today they are not willing to sell bonds, the trader said.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract was down 30/32 at 114-5/32. The March T-bond contract was down 1-10/32 at 110-3/32. The MOB spread was 130 ticks.
